treks.name: Bhadraj Temple Trek
treks.description: A gentle forest walk from Mussoorie to one of the region's oldest temples dedicated to Lord Bal Bhadra (Krishna's brother). The trail passes through dense oak and deodar forests with views of the Yamuna valley and Doon valley stretching to the horizon. Ideal for families and first-time trekkers.
highlights: Ancient Bhadraj Temple with panoramic Doon Valley views
Dense oak and deodar forest canopy
Views of Yamuna valley and distant Himalayan peaks
warnings: Trail can be slippery after rain
Monkeys in forested sections — keep food packed
No shops after Hathipaon — carry water and snacks
Return before dark as trail is poorly marked

day_by_day_first.meals: Carry packed lunch. Nothing available on trail.
day_by_day_first.title: Hathipaon to Bhadraj Temple
day_by_day_first.water: Small stream at 2km mark (seasonal). Carry 2L from Mussoorie.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail through oak and deodar, gentle gradient with a few short steep sections. Well-trodden path.
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Hathipaon estate on Mussoorie-Yamuna Bridge road. The trail enters oak forest immediately, climbing gently. Pass through small clearings with valley views. At 3km mark, trail forks — take right for Bhadraj. Dense deodar section before final clearing with the temple. Views open up dramatically at the top. Return same route.

treks.nearest_hospital: Landour Community Hospital — 8km from trailhead, 30 minutes by road. Doon Hospital Dehradun — 35km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio and Airtel work for most of the trail. Signal drops in dense forest sections. Good coverage at temple.

treks.name: Singalila Ridge Trek
treks.description: A 5-day ridge walk through Singalila National Park along the India-Nepal border with continuous views of the Kanchenjunga range. Shorter and more focused than the Sandakphu-Phalut circuit, this trek stays on the ridge for maximum mountain exposure. Spring transforms the trail into a rhododendron wonderland. Trekkers' huts along the route provide comfortable shelter.
highlights: Continuous Kanchenjunga range views for 5 days
Rhododendron forests in spectacular spring bloom
Comfortable trekkers' huts along the route
Sandakphu summit — highest point in West Bengal
Less crowded than the full Sandakphu-Phalut circuit
warnings: Cold temperatures at ridge camps (below -5°C in winter)
Permits required for Singalila National Park
Weather can obscure views — allow buffer days

day_by_day_first.meals: Tea house meals
day_by_day_first.title: Manebhanjan to Tumling
day_by_day_first.water: Tea houses
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail, jeep track, steep sections
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Manebhanjan and climb through forest into Singalila National Park. Reach Tumling on the India-Nepal border.

treks.nearest_hospital: Darjeeling District Hospital — 60km from Manebhanjan, 3 hours. Basic first aid at Sandakphu.
treks.network_coverage: Patchy Airtel/Jio at Tumling and Sandakphu. No coverage between stops.

treks.name: Gandikota Canyon Trek
treks.description: Trek along the Pennar River gorge rim and down to the river level.

treks.name: Pin Parvati Pass
treks.description: Cross from Parvati Valley to Spiti over 5319m pass. India classic high-altitude crossing.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Nakthan. Dinner at Kheerganga camp
day_by_day_first.title: Barsheni to Kheerganga
day_by_day_first.water: Parvati river. Hot springs (not for drinking)
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail along Parvati river
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Bhuntar to Barsheni. Trek along Parvati river through forest. Pass Rudra Nag waterfall. Reach Kheerganga hot springs. Soak and rest.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Jari 15km from Barsheni (Parvati side). Zero medical facilities for 7 days. Mudh has no medical facility. Kaza has PHC. Serious cases: Kullu 50km or Keylong 80km. Helicopter evacuation extremely difficult in upper valley.
treks.network_coverage: Jio at Barsheni. Zero signal from Kheerganga to Mudh (9 days of complete isolation). This is one of India's most remote crossings. Satellite phone MANDATORY.

treks.name: Tarsar Marsar Trek
treks.description: Twin alpine lake trek through Kashmir — the most scenic trek in the valley.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch enroute Pahalgam. Dinner at Aru
day_by_day_first.title: Srinagar to Aru Valley
day_by_day_first.water: Village water. River at Aru
day_by_day_first.terrain: Road journey
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Srinagar to Aru Valley via Pahalgam (95km, 4hr). Aru is a picturesque meadow village with gujjar settlements. Register with local guide. Overnight at Aru guesthouse or camp.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Aru area. District Hospital Pahalgam 12km from Aru. Serious cases: SKIMS Srinagar 95km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Aru and Pahalgam. No signal from Lidderwat onwards. Zero coverage at lakes. BSNL very patchy at Lidderwat only.

treks.name: Triund Trek
treks.description: Most popular day trek in Himachal — 9km return to Dhauladhar ridge.

day_by_day_first.meals: Maggi and chai at trail cafes. Dinner at Triund camp dhabas
day_by_day_first.title: McLeodganj to Triund
day_by_day_first.water: Multiple chai shops on trail. Carry 1L minimum for summit push
day_by_day_first.terrain: Well-marked rocky trail through oak and rhododendron forest
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Galu Devi Temple near Dharamkot. Steady climb through dense forest. Trail widens after Magic View Cafe. Final 1km is steep rocky switchbacks. Stunning Dhauladhar views at top.

treks.nearest_hospital: Zonal Hospital McLeodganj 9km. Serious cases: Fortis Hospital Kangra 30km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel works till Dharamkot. Patchy signal at Magic View Cafe. Intermittent Jio at Triund Top. BSNL best coverage.

treks.name: Mullayyanagiri Trek
treks.description: Trek to the highest peak in Karnataka. Easy trail from Sarpadhari viewpoint to the summit temple.
treks.nearest_hospital: Government Hospital Chikmagalur 30km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio at Sarpadhari. Weak signal at summit.

treks.name: Kolahoi Glacier Trek
treks.description: Trek to Kashmir largest glacier from Pahalgam via Lidderwat.

day_by_day_first.meals: Breakfast at Srinagar. Lunch on trail. Dinner at camp
day_by_day_first.title: Srinagar to Aru to Lidderwat
day_by_day_first.water: Lidder river alongside trail. Stream at camp
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail along Lidder river
day_by_day_first.description: Drive Srinagar to Aru (4hr). Trek along Lidder river through pine forest. Gentle climb to Lidderwat - a stunning meadow at river confluence. Classic Kashmir basecamp.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Aru area. District Hospital Pahalgam 12km. Serious cases: SKIMS Srinagar 95km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Aru. Weak BSNL at Lidderwat. No signal from Satlanjan onwards. Zero coverage near glacier.

treks.name: Goecha La Approach (Yuksom to Dzongri)
treks.description: A shorter, more accessible version of the legendary Goechala Trek, ending at Dzongri viewpoint (3680m) instead of pushing to the pass. Perfect for trekkers who want Kanchenjunga views and rhododendron forests without the extreme altitude and 10-day commitment. Dzongri Top offers a stunning 360-degree panorama of Sikkim's highest peaks.
highlights: Rhododendron forests in spectacular spring bloom
Shorter 4-day version of the legendary Goechala trek
Accessible introduction to high-altitude Sikkim trekking
warnings: No mobile network from Day 2 onwards
Permits required — allow 2 days processing in Yuksom
Trail is shared with Goechala trekkers — can be busy in season

day_by_day_first.meals: Packed lunch, camp dinner
day_by_day_first.title: Yuksom to Sachen
day_by_day_first.water: Multiple streams
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail through subtropical forest
day_by_day_first.description: Begin at Yuksom (1780m). Enter Kanchenjunga National Park and climb through dense forest.

treks.nearest_hospital: Namchi District Hospital — 110km from Yuksom, 5 hours. Yuksom has a basic health center.
treks.network_coverage: No network from Day 2. Jio/Airtel work in Yuksom only.

treks.name: Kedarkantha Winter Trek
treks.description: India most popular winter trek. Guaranteed snow.

day_by_day_first.meals: Breakfast at Dehradun. Lunch enroute at Purola. Dinner at Sankri homestay
day_by_day_first.title: Dehradun to Sankri
day_by_day_first.water: Shops at Sankri
day_by_day_first.terrain: Road journey
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Dehradun to Sankri (1920m) via Mussoorie, Purola, Mori. 10hr scenic drive through Govind National Park area. Register at forest office. Overnight at guesthouse.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Sankri 4km. CHC Purola 50km. Serious cases: District Hospital Uttarkashi 80km or Dehradun 200km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL at Sankri (weak). Jio at Sankri (intermittent). No signal at Juda Ka Talab, base camp, or summit. Zero coverage on trail.

treks.name: Kumara Parvatha Trek
treks.description: The toughest trek in Karnataka. Pushpagiri range through Kukke Subramanya to the summit. Steep, exposed, and breathtaking. Dense shola forests to open grasslands.
treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Kukke Subramanya 12km. Nearest hospital: Sullia 40km. Serious: Mangalore 100km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL at Kukke Subramanya. Zero coverage on trek after Bhattara Mane.

treks.name: Nandi Hills Sunrise Trek
treks.description: Popular sunrise trek from the base of Nandi Hills. Stunning sunrise above clouds on winter mornings.
treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Nandi Hills. Nearest hospital: Chikkaballapur 12km.
treks.network_coverage: Full Jio/Airtel coverage.

treks.name: Srisailam Nallamala Forest Trek
treks.description: Forest trek through Nallamala Hills near Srisailam.

treks.name: Deoria Tal to Chandrashila
treks.description: Combine Deoria Tal reflection lake with Tungnath temple and Chandrashila summit.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Sari. Dinner at camp
day_by_day_first.title: Sari Village to Deoria Tal
day_by_day_first.water: Deoria Tal lake (purify). Seasonal stream near camp
day_by_day_first.terrain: Steep forest trail with stone steps
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Rishikesh/Ukhimath to Sari village (1920m). Short but steep climb through dense forest. Deoria Tal is a pristine emerald lake reflecting Chaukhamba peaks. Camp by the lake - one of the most photographed campsites in Uttarakhand.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Chopta (basic). CHC Ukhimath 25km. Serious cases: District Hospital Rudraprayag 60km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL at Sari village. No signal at Deoria Tal or Rohini Bugyal. BSNL patchy at Chopta. Jio at Chopta only.

treks.name: Hampta Pass Trek
treks.description: Cross from green Kullu to barren Lahaul in 4 days. Classic intro to Himalayan trekking.

day_by_day_first.meals: Breakfast at Manali. Lunch on trail. Dinner at camp
day_by_day_first.title: Manali to Jobra to Chikka
day_by_day_first.water: Rani Nallah stream alongside trail. Stream at Chikka camp
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail along Rani Nallah stream
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Manali to Jobra (2700m, 30min). Trek starts along Rani Nallah through dense birch and maple forest. Gradual ascent through beautiful valley. Cross wooden bridge over stream. Reach Chikka campsite in a valley bowl.

treks.nearest_hospital: Civil Hospital Manali 15km from Jobra. On Lahaul side: PHC Chatru 5km from Shea Goru. Serious cases: Keylong Hospital 60km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Jobra. No signal from Chikka onwards until Chatru. Chatru has weak BSNL. Zero coverage at pass.

treks.name: Kuari Pass Trek
treks.description: Lord Curzon trail with Nanda Devi views throughout.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Auli. Dinner at camp
day_by_day_first.title: Auli to Gorson Bugyal
day_by_day_first.water: Spring near Gorson camp
day_by_day_first.terrain: Gentle meadow trail from Auli ski slopes
day_by_day_first.description: Reach Auli from Joshimath by ropeway or road. Short walk through Auli meadows to Gorson Bugyal. Stunning views of Nanda Devi, Dronagiri, Hathi Parvat. Easy acclimatization day.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Auli 5km. CHC Joshimath 10km. Serious cases: District Hospital Chamoli 60km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/BSNL at Joshimath and Auli. Patchy at Gorson. No signal at Tali or Kuari Pass.

treks.name: Lambasingi Cloud Forest Walk
treks.description: Walk through cloud-wrapped Eastern Ghats forest above Lambasingi.
warnings: Sub-zero temperatures — carry heavy winter gear

treks.name: Bhongir Fort Scramble
treks.description: Scramble up the egg-shaped monolithic rock to the 10th-century fort summit.

treks.name: Ananthagiri Hills Forest Trek
treks.description: Easy forest walk through deciduous forest above Vikarabad.

treks.name: Horsley Hills Nature Walk
treks.description: Gentle forest walk through eucalyptus and mahogany plantation forests.
warnings: Trail can be slippery in monsoon

treks.name: Indrahar Pass Trek
treks.description: The crown jewel beyond Triund — Indrahar Pass at 4342m is the gateway from Kangra valley to Chamba. Standing at the pass, you see the lush green Kangra valley on one side and the stark, dramatic Chamba landscape on the other. The climb from Triund involves steep snow sections and requires good fitness, but the reward is one of the most dramatic pass crossings in Himachal.
highlights: Gateway pass between Kangra and Chamba valleys
Dramatic landscape change visible from the pass
Snow wall climb near the pass — thrilling
Dhauladhar range up close and personal
Far less crowded than nearby treks
warnings: Pass crossing requires good fitness and prior experience
Snow on approach even in September — crampons may be needed
AMS risk above 4000m — acclimatize at Lahesh Cave
Weather at pass is unpredictable — turn back if clouds build
Trail from Lahesh Cave to pass is steep and exposed
Guide essential — trail not marked above Lahesh Cave
Do NOT attempt in monsoon — extremely dangerous

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at trail cafes. Dinner at Triund dhabas.
day_by_day_first.title: McLeodganj to Triund
day_by_day_first.water: Multiple chai shops on trail. Water at Triund camp.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Well-marked forest trail. Rocky switchbacks in final section.
day_by_day_first.description: Standard Triund trek from Galu Devi Temple. Through oak and rhododendron forest with Dhauladhar views opening up. Camp at Triund — the launchpad for Indrahar Pass.

treks.nearest_hospital: Dharamshala Zonal Hospital — 10km from McLeodganj, 30 minutes by road
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel work at Triund (weak). No signal at Lahesh Cave or pass. Completely off-grid above Triund.

treks.name: Kheerganga Trek
treks.description: Trek to natural hot springs at 2960m in Parvati Valley.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Nakthan village dhaba. Dinner at Kheerganga camps (Israeli/Indian food available)
day_by_day_first.title: Barshaini to Kheerganga
day_by_day_first.water: Parvati river and streams throughout. Carry 1L
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail with river crossings, some exposed sections
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Barshaini (2100m). Cross Parvati river on bridge. Trail follows Parvati valley through dense forest. Pass Rudra Nag waterfall at midpoint. Final steep section through meadows to Kheerganga hot springs. Soak in natural hot water pools.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Jari 15km from Barshaini. Serious cases: Regional Hospital Kullu 50km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio at Barshaini. No signal on trail. Faint BSNL at Kheerganga. Airtel absent throughout.

treks.name: Rupin Pass Trek
treks.description: Cross from Shimla side to Kinnaur via 4650m pass with hanging glacier waterfall.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch enroute. Dinner at Dhaula homestay
day_by_day_first.title: Shimla/Rohru to Dhaula
day_by_day_first.water: Village water supply
day_by_day_first.terrain: Road journey to trailhead
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Shimla to Rohru (6hr) then to Dhaula village (2100m). Register and meet local guide. Stay at village homestay. Trek briefing.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Jiskun area (seasonal). CHC Rohru 50km (Shimla side). CHC Sangla 12km (Kinnaur side). Serious cases: IGMC Shimla 150km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL at Dhaula and Sewa (weak). No signal from Jiskun to Ronti Gad. Jio/Airtel at Sangla. Zero coverage on pass.

treks.name: Rajmachi Fort Trek
treks.description: Twin forts of Shrivardhan and Manaranjan perched on the Sahyadri ridge. The trek from Lonavala via Udhewadi passes through dense forest. Monsoon transforms the trail with waterfalls and greenery.
highlights: Twin Maratha forts with panoramic views
Night trek popular with Mumbai/Pune trekkers
warnings: Path unclear in fog — use GPS

treks.name: Sar Pass Trek
treks.description: Cross the Sar Pass from Parvati Valley with snow corridors and pine forests.

day_by_day_first.meals: Breakfast at Kasol. Lunch on trail. Dinner at Grahan homestay
day_by_day_first.title: Kasol to Grahan
day_by_day_first.water: Parvati river at start. Streams on trail. Village tap water at Grahan
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail along river, then steep climb to village
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Kasol bridge. Follow Parvati river briefly then climb steeply through pine and oak forest. Reach Grahan - a beautiful hamlet with wooden houses, temple, and apple orchards. Homestay in village.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Kasol 8km from Grahan. Regional Hospital Kullu 55km. Serious cases: Kullu hospital.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Kasol. Patchy BSNL at Grahan. No signal from Min Thatch onwards until Barshaini.

treks.name: Harishchandragad Trek (Konkan Kada)
treks.description: One of Maharashtra's most dramatic treks. Konkan Kada is a concave cliff face overhanging a 1,400m vertical drop — standing at the edge is one of India's most thrilling experiences. Multiple routes: Pachnai (easiest), Nalichi Vaat (rock patch), Junnar Darwaza.
highlights: Konkan Kada — overhanging cliff with 1400m drop
Kedareshwar cave temple with Shiva linga surrounded by water
warnings: Konkan Kada edge has NO railing — fatal falls have occurred
Nalichi Vaat route requires rock climbing
No phone signal on most of the trek

treks.name: Maredumilli Waterfall Trek
treks.description: Tribal-guided trek through semi-evergreen forest to waterfalls.

treks.name: Milam Glacier Trek
treks.description: Multi-day trek to one of India largest glaciers. Inner Line Permit required.

day_by_day_first.meals: Road dhabas. Dinner at Munsiyari
day_by_day_first.title: Kathgodam to Munsiyari
day_by_day_first.water: Town water supply
day_by_day_first.terrain: Road journey
day_by_day_first.description: Train to Kathgodam, then drive to Munsiyari (10hr) via Almora and Birthi Falls. Munsiyari offers stunning Panchachuli range views. Rest and acclimatize. Register at ITBP checkpoint.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Munsiyari at start/end. Zero medical facilities between Lilam and Milam. Serious cases: District Hospital Pithoragarh 90km. Helicopter evacuation difficult in narrow valley.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL at Munsiyari (weak). No signal from Lilam to Milam (8 days). This is one of India's most remote treks. Satellite phone essential.

treks.name: Kalsubai Peak Trek
treks.description: Maharashtra's highest peak at 1,646m. The trek from Bari village follows a well-marked trail with iron ladders on steep rock sections. The summit has a small temple and 360-degree views of the Sahyadri range and Arthur Lake.
highlights: Views of Bhandardara reservoir and Sahyadri range
warnings: Iron ladders can be slippery in rain
Start early (6am) to avoid afternoon clouds
Carry 3L water — no water sources on trail

treks.name: Gandhamardan Hills Twin Temple Trek
treks.description: 16km plateau walk connecting Nrusinghanath and Harishankar temples through Gandhamardan Hills. Buddhist ruins en route.

treks.name: Satkosia Gorge Nature Trail
treks.description: Guided nature trail along the rim of Satkosia gorge with views of the Mahanadi River below. Gharial spotting from viewpoints.

treks.name: Daringbadi Pine Forest Walk
treks.description: Easy walk through Daringbadi pine forests and coffee gardens. Tribal village visits possible with guide.

treks.name: Ali Bedni Bugyal
treks.description: Trek to one of India largest alpine meadows — Bedni Bugyal at 3354m with Nanda Ghunti views.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Lohajung. Dinner at Didna homestay (home-cooked Garhwali food)
day_by_day_first.title: Lohajung to Didna Village
day_by_day_first.water: Village tap water. Stream near Didna
day_by_day_first.terrain: Village trail through terraced fields and forest
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Rishikesh to Lohajung (2250m, 10hr). Trek descends slightly then climbs through beautiful terraced villages. Didna is a small Garhwali village with homestays. Acclimatize here.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Wan Village 9km from Bedni. CHC Tharali 45km. Serious cases: District Hospital Chamoli 80km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL at Lohajung and Didna (weak). Zero signal at Ali Bugyal and Bedni Bugyal. Jio/Airtel absent on trail.

treks.name: Beas Kund Trek
treks.description: Easy trek to the glacial source of the Beas River near Manali.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch packed from Manali. Dinner at camp
day_by_day_first.title: Solang Valley to Bakarthach
day_by_day_first.water: Multiple stream crossings. Beas river tributary alongside trail
day_by_day_first.terrain: Gradual forest trail along Beas river tributary
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Manali to Solang Valley (2480m). Trek begins past the ropeway station. Gentle ascent through silver birch and pine forest. Cross small streams. Reach Bakarthach meadow by afternoon.

treks.nearest_hospital: Civil Hospital Manali 15km. Serious cases: Regional Hospital Kullu 55km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Solang Valley. No signal beyond Solang. Zero coverage at Bakarthach and Beas Kund.

treks.name: Bhrigu Lake Trek
treks.description: Trek to a sacred glacial lake at 4300m near Manali.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch packed from Manali. Dinner at camp
day_by_day_first.title: Gulaba to Rola Kholi
day_by_day_first.water: Stream at Rola Kholi campsite. Small streams on trail
day_by_day_first.terrain: Grassy meadow trail with gradual ascent
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Manali to Gulaba (2800m) on Rohtang road. Trek through lush green meadows dotted with wildflowers. Gradual climb with views of Pir Panjal range. Camp at Rola Kholi, a beautiful meadow beside a stream.

treks.nearest_hospital: Civil Hospital Manali 20km. Serious cases: Regional Hospital Kullu 60km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio at Gulaba (on Rohtang road). No signal at Rola Kholi or above. Zero coverage at Bhrigu Lake.

treks.name: Lohagad Fort Trek
treks.description: One of Maharashtra's most accessible fort treks. Well-paved steps lead to the top of Lohagad (Iron Fort), with panoramic views of Pawna Lake and the surrounding Sahyadri hills. Connected to Visapur Fort via a saddle.
highlights: Pawna Lake views from the top
Connected to Visapur Fort — do both in a day

treks.name: Brahmatal Winter Trek
treks.description: Winter trek to two frozen lakes with Trishul views.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Lohajung. Dinner at camp
day_by_day_first.title: Lohajung to Bekaltal
day_by_day_first.water: Bekaltal lake (purify). Small stream near campsite
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail through oak and rhododendron
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Rishikesh to Lohajung (2250m, 10hr). Start trek through dense forest. Gentle climb with occasional clearings showing Trishul and Nanda Ghunti peaks. Reach Bekaltal - a serene forest lake, frozen in winter.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Wan Village 6km from Brahmatal. CHC Tharali 40km. Serious cases: District Hospital Chamoli 80km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL at Lohajung (weak). No signal at Bekaltal, Brahmatal, or summit. Jio/Airtel absent. Zero coverage on entire trail.

treks.name: Chadar Trek
treks.description: Walk on frozen Zanskar River for 62km over 9 days at -25C.

day_by_day_first.meals: Light meals at Leh. Avoid heavy food
day_by_day_first.title: Leh acclimatization
day_by_day_first.water: Bottled water from shops
day_by_day_first.terrain: Rest day
day_by_day_first.description: Arrive in Leh. MANDATORY acclimatization day. Do not exert. Walk slowly. Drink 3-4L water. Visit Leh Palace or Shanti Stupa gently. Altitude sickness is the biggest risk on this trek.

treks.nearest_hospital: Zero medical facilities on entire route. Nearest: SNM Hospital Leh 3-6hr walk + drive. Helicopter evacuation extremely difficult in narrow gorge. Medical kit must be comprehensive. Operator should carry oxygen cylinder.
treks.network_coverage: Zero signal on entire chadar. No BSNL, no Jio, no Airtel from Chilling to Nerak and back (7-8 days). Satellite phone MANDATORY. Register your satellite phone IMEI with DoT India before trek.

treks.name: Sandakphu-Phalut Trek
treks.description: The only place on earth where you can see four of the world's five highest peaks in a single panorama — Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, and Makalu. Walking along the India-Nepal border ridge through Singalila National Park, this trek rewards with the famous "Sleeping Buddha" silhouette formed by the Kanchenjunga range. Rhododendron forests explode in color during spring.
highlights: Only place to see 4 of world's 5 highest peaks simultaneously
Famous Sleeping Giant/Sleeping Buddha view of Kanchenjunga range
Spring rhododendron forests in spectacular bloom
Sandakphu — highest point in West Bengal at 3636m
warnings: Extremely cold at Sandakphu/Phalut in winter (below -10°C)
Land Rover tracks can be dusty — not a wilderness trail
Weather can close views for days — allow buffer days

day_by_day_first.meals: Tea house meals available
day_by_day_first.title: Manebhanjan to Tumling
day_by_day_first.water: Tea houses
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail with steep sections, jeep track
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Manebhanjan (2134m). Climb through Chitrey and dense forest. Cross into Singalila National Park. Tumling sits on the India-Nepal border.

treks.nearest_hospital: Darjeeling District Hospital — 60km from Manebhanjan, 3 hours. Basic first aid at Sandakphu.
treks.network_coverage: Patchy Airtel/Jio at Tumling and Sandakphu. No coverage between stops and at Phalut.

treks.name: Pachmarhi Nature Trail
treks.description: Forest walk through Satpura Hills to Bee Falls and Pandava Caves. MP only hill station.

treks.name: Great Himalayan Trail
treks.description: Multi-section traverse of the entire Himalayan range across multiple states.

day_by_day_first.meals: Road dhabas
day_by_day_first.title: Nainital to Munsiyari (Kumaon Start)
day_by_day_first.water: Town water
day_by_day_first.terrain: Road journey to eastern starting point
day_by_day_first.description: Drive or take shared transport to Munsiyari (10-12hr). GHT Indian section typically starts from eastern Kumaon. Acclimatize. Register with local authorities. Meet guide team.

treks.nearest_hospital: Resupply towns have PHC/CHC: Munsiyari, Joshimath (best), Ghangaria (seasonal), Har Ki Dun area (Osla), Chitkul, Kasol, Manali. Between towns: zero medical facilities for 3-5 day stretches. Helicopter evacuation possible from meadows only. Comprehensive medical kit and trained first-aider in team mandatory.
treks.network_coverage: Signal at resupply towns only: Munsiyari (BSNL), Joshimath (all networks), Ghangaria (BSNL weak), Chitkul (BSNL), Kasol (Jio/Airtel), Manali (all). Zero signal for 3-7 day stretches between towns. Satellite phone MANDATORY for entire route.

treks.name: Great Lakes of Kashmir
treks.description: Seven alpine lakes in 7 days — Kashmir most epic multi-day trek.

day_by_day_first.meals: Breakfast at Srinagar. Lunch on trail. Dinner at camp
day_by_day_first.title: Srinagar to Sonamarg to Nichnai
day_by_day_first.water: Streams every 1-2km. Nichnai stream at camp
day_by_day_first.terrain: Well-trodden path through pine forest and meadows
day_by_day_first.description: Drive Srinagar to Sonamarg (80km, 3hr). Trek starts from Sonamarg. Gradual ascent through pine forest and alpine meadows. Nichnai is a beautiful camp in a meadow bowl surrounded by mountains.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Sonamarg (entry). PHC Naranag area (exit). Serious cases: SKIMS Srinagar 80km. Helicopter evacuation possible from open meadows.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Sonamarg. Zero signal from Nichnai to Naranag (6 days). Occasional BSNL blip at high passes. Satellite phone recommended.

treks.name: David Scott Trail
treks.description: A colonial-era horse trail built by David Scott, the first British administrator of the Khasi and Jaintia Hills, to connect Assam with Bangladesh (then Sylhet). This gentle 16km walk through pine and oak forests, past streams, and through traditional Khasi villages offers a window into Meghalaya's living cultural landscape. One of the most accessible and rewarding treks in Northeast India.
highlights: Colonial-era horse trail with historical significance
Pine and oak forests with moss-covered canopy
Crystal-clear streams with natural swimming spots
Traditional Khasi villages along the route
One of Northeast India's most accessible treks
warnings: Trail can be muddy and slippery in monsoon (Jun-Sep)
Limited shade in open sections — carry sun protection
No shops or eateries on trail — carry all food and water
Some stream crossings may be tricky after rain
Return transport from endpoint needs pre-arrangement

day_by_day_first.meals: Carry packed lunch and snacks
day_by_day_first.title: Mawphlang to Lad Mawphlang
day_by_day_first.water: Multiple streams — purify before drinking
day_by_day_first.terrain: Gentle forest trail, some stream crossings, grassland sections
day_by_day_first.description: Start near Mawphlang Sacred Grove. The trail follows the old horse path through pine forests, crossing several streams. Pass through open grasslands with views of the Khasi Hills. Enter oak forest sections draped in moss. Cross through small Khasi hamlets. End at Lad Mawphlang village where pre-arranged transport waits.

treks.nearest_hospital: Shillong Civil Hospital — 25km from Mawphlang, 1 hour by road.
treks.network_coverage: Airtel and Jio work at Mawphlang. Patchy coverage mid-trail. Signal returns at Lad Mawphlang.

treks.name: Chandrashila Summit
treks.description: Easiest 4000m summit in India. 360-degree Himalayan panorama.

day_by_day_first.meals: Breakfast at Chopta dhaba. Carry packed lunch. Prasad at Tungnath temple. Dinner at Chopta
day_by_day_first.title: Chopta to Chandrashila Summit
day_by_day_first.water: Carry 2L from Chopta. Small shop at Tungnath (seasonal). No water on summit ridge
day_by_day_first.terrain: Stone steps to Tungnath, then rocky scramble to summit
day_by_day_first.campsite: None - day trek, return to Chopta
day_by_day_first.description: Start early from Chopta (3000m). Well-paved stone path to Tungnath temple (3680m, highest Shiva temple). From Tungnath, steep rocky ridge trail to Chandrashila summit. 360-degree panorama of Nanda Devi, Trishul, Kedarnath, Chaukhamba, Bandarpunch. Return same day to Chopta.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Chopta 0km (basic). CHC Ukhimath 25km. Serious cases: District Hospital Rudraprayag 60km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL works at Chopta. Jio patchy. No signal at Tungnath or summit. Airtel at Chopta only.

treks.name: Deomali Peak Summit Trek
treks.description: Trek to Odisha's highest point at 1,672m through Eastern Ghats tribal country. Paved road halfway, final section is steep climbing.

treks.name: Khaliya Top Trek
treks.description: Day trek to Panchachuli viewpoint from Munsiyari.

day_by_day_first.meals: Breakfast at Munsiyari. Carry packed lunch. Dinner at Munsiyari
day_by_day_first.title: Munsiyari to Khaliya Top and return
day_by_day_first.water: Forest spring at 2km. No water above treeline - carry 2L
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail through rhododendron and oak, final stretch through alpine meadow
day_by_day_first.campsite: None - return to Munsiyari (can camp at Khaliya meadow)
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Munsiyari (2700m). Trail begins near KMVN guesthouse. Climb through dense rhododendron forest (spectacular in March-April with red blooms). Above treeline, open bugyals (meadows) with 180-degree Panchachuli range view. Summit offers views of Nanda Devi East, Rajrambha, Hardeol.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Munsiyari 0km. Serious cases: District Hospital Pithoragarh 90km (4hr drive).
treks.network_coverage: BSNL at Munsiyari town. Jio patchy. No signal on trail or at Khaliya Top. Airtel absent.

treks.name: Nag Tibba Trek
treks.description: Highest peak in lower Garhwal — easy weekend trek from Delhi.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Pantwari dhaba. Dinner at camp (guide provides or self-cook)
day_by_day_first.title: Pantwari to Nag Tibba Base Camp
day_by_day_first.water: Stream crossing at 2km mark. Seasonal spring near base camp
day_by_day_first.terrain: Moderate forest trail through oak and deodar
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Dehradun/Mussoorie to Pantwari village (1900m). Register at forest checkpoint. Trail winds through dense forest with gradual ascent. Reach base camp clearing by afternoon. Set up camp with Himalayan views.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Nainbagh 15km. CHC Mussoorie 30km. Serious cases: Doon Hospital Dehradun 60km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Pantwari village. No signal at base camp or summit. BSNL very patchy throughout.

treks.name: Sinhagad Fort Trek
treks.description: Pune's most beloved trek. Sinhagad (Lion Fort) is where Tanaji Malusare scaled the cliff face with a monitor lizard to recapture it for Shivaji — "Gad aala pan Sinha gela" (the fort is won but the lion is lost). The monsoon trek from the base is stunning.
highlights: Easy monsoon trek with waterfall crossings
warnings: Road to top closed in heavy monsoon — trek only
Parking lot fills by 8am on weekends

treks.name: Valley of Flowers Trek
treks.description: Trek to UNESCO valley with 500+ wildflower species.

day_by_day_first.meals: Breakfast at Govindghat. Lunch at Bhyundar midway. Dinner at Ghangaria hotel
day_by_day_first.title: Govindghat to Ghangaria
day_by_day_first.water: Multiple streams and chai shops along route. River alongside
day_by_day_first.terrain: Paved path along Lakshman Ganga river, mule track available
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Govindghat (1828m) on Joshimath-Badrinath road. Well-maintained paved/stone path along Lakshman Ganga river. Steady climb through gorge. Helicopter option available (Rs 3500). Ghangaria is base for both Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib.

treks.nearest_hospital: Medical post at Ghangaria (basic, seasonal). PHC Govindghat. Serious cases: District Hospital Chamoli 60km or Joshimath CHC 25km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL at Ghangaria (intermittent). Jio weak. No signal inside Valley of Flowers. Airtel absent. Best coverage at Govindghat.

treks.name: Roopkund Mystery Lake
treks.description: Trek to the mysterious skeleton lake at 4800m — hundreds of human skeletons visible when snow melts.

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Lohajung. Dinner at camp
day_by_day_first.title: Lohajung to Wan Village to Bedni Bugyal
day_by_day_first.water: Village water at Wan. Forest streams. Bedni Kund lake (purify)
day_by_day_first.terrain: Village trail then steep forest climb to alpine meadow
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Rishikesh to Lohajung (10hr). Trek to Wan village then steep climb through forest to Bedni Bugyal. Vast alpine meadow with Bedni Kund (sacred lake). Acclimatize at this stunning campsite.

treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Wan Village. CHC Tharali 45km. Serious cases: District Hospital Chamoli 80km. Helicopter evacuation possible from Bedni Bugyal.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL weak at Lohajung. Zero signal from Wan village onwards. No coverage at any campsite or Roopkund. Satellite phone recommended for emergencies.

treks.name: Torna Fort Trek
treks.description: Shivaji's first fort — he captured Torna at age 16 in 1643, beginning the Maratha Empire. The highest fort in the Pune district at 1,404m. The trek from Velhe village is steep but rewarding with views of Rajgad and the surrounding Sahyadri.
highlights: Views of Rajgad Fort across the valley

treks.name: Bijli Mahadev Trek
treks.description: A short but rewarding trek to one of Himachal's most dramatic temples — Bijli Mahadev — where lightning strikes the Shiva lingam and the priest reassembles it with butter. The panoramic ridge walk offers jaw-dropping views of Kullu, Parvati, and Garsa valleys with the Beas River snaking below.
highlights: Lightning-struck Shiva lingam reassembled with butter
360-degree views of Kullu, Parvati and Garsa valleys
One of the easiest ridge treks in Himachal
Ancient temple at 2460m with fascinating legend
Beas River valley panorama at sunset
warnings: Trail is exposed — avoid during thunderstorms
No water source on the trail — carry from base
Last section is steep stone steps
Monkeys near the temple can snatch food
Return before dark — trail not marked for night hiking

day_by_day_first.meals: Carry packed lunch. Small shop at Chansari for biscuits and water.
day_by_day_first.title: Chansari Village to Bijli Mahadev Temple
day_by_day_first.water: No water on trail. Carry 1.5L from Chansari.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Paved road for first 1km then stone steps and dirt trail along ridge. Final approach is steep stone steps.
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Kullu to Chansari village (25km, 45min). The trek begins at the road end. First section follows a gentle incline through apple orchards and deodar forest. After 2km the trail opens onto a grassy ridge with stunning valley views. Final 500m is a steep climb up stone steps to the temple. Spend time at the temple, enjoy the views, and return the same way.

treks.nearest_hospital: Regional Hospital Kullu — 25km from Chansari, 45 minutes by road
treks.network_coverage: Jio and Airtel work at temple top. BSNL intermittent. Good signal at Chansari.

treks.name: Chandra Tal Lake Trek
treks.description: The crescent-shaped Moon Lake of Spiti sits at 4300m surrounded by stark brown mountains that reflect perfectly in its turquoise waters. While reachable by a short 2km walk from the parking lot, the altitude makes it deceptively challenging. One of the most photogenic high-altitude lakes in India — every angle is a postcard.
highlights: Perfect mountain reflections in still morning water
Stark Spiti landscape — feels like another planet
One of India's highest accessible lakes
Stargazing at campsite is extraordinary — zero light pollution
warnings: High altitude — acclimatize in Kaza for 2 days minimum before visiting
AMS risk is real even for a short walk — descend immediately if headache/nausea
Road to parking lot is rough and only open June-September
Camping rules are strict — designated spots only, no littering
Weather changes rapidly — carry warm layers even in summer
No medical help nearby — nearest hospital is Kaza 70km away

day_by_day_first.meals: All meals self-arranged or through camping operators who set up parachute tents with kitchen.
day_by_day_first.title: Chandra Tal Parking to Lake and Return
day_by_day_first.water: Stream near campsite. Lake water is clean but purify to be safe. Carry 2L.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Flat to gently undulating trail across marshy ground and rocky moraine. Boardwalks installed in marshy sections.
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Kaza to Batal (65km, 3hrs on rough road) then to Chandra Tal parking (14km further, 1hr). The walk from parking to lake is 2km on a well-marked trail. Cross marshy sections on boardwalks, then rocky moraine before the lake appears. Spend time at the lake — mornings offer mirror reflections. Return same route. Camping overnight at designated campsite 2km before lake.

treks.nearest_hospital: Community Health Center Kaza — 70km, 3 hours by road. For serious cases, Rampur Hospital 200km.
treks.network_coverage: No mobile network at Chandra Tal. BSNL occasionally works at Batal. Kaza has BSNL coverage.

treks.name: Har Ki Dun Trek
treks.description: A cradle-shaped valley at the foot of Swargarohini peak — the mountain where the Pandavas are believed to have ascended to heaven. Har Ki Dun is one of the few treks that combines ancient mythology, stunning alpine meadows, and living Himalayan culture in villages that still follow traditions dating back centuries. The trail passes through gorgeous forests and traditional Himalayan hamlets.
highlights: Swargarohini peak views — mythological ascent of Pandavas
Ancient timber villages of Osla and Seema with pagoda temples
Vast alpine meadows carpeted in wildflowers (May-June)
Rich wildlife — Himalayan monal, musk deer sightings possible
One of the best moderate treks accessible to families
warnings: Inner Line Permit required from Uttarkashi DM office
Stream crossings can be tricky after rain — use trekking poles
Bears have been sighted — make noise on trail
Osla village has strict cultural norms — dress respectfully at temple
Weather changes fast in valley — carry rain gear always

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch packed from Sankri. Dinner at homestay or campsite.
day_by_day_first.title: Sankri to Taluka
day_by_day_first.water: Supin river accessible throughout. Streams at regular intervals.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Gentle trail through pine forest along Supin river. Some road walking initially.
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Sankri village. Follow the Supin river valley through mixed pine and oak forest. The trail is mostly flat with gentle undulations. Pass through small hamlets. Taluka is a small village with homestays and camping ground.

treks.nearest_hospital: District Hospital Uttarkashi — 95km from Sankri, 4 hours by road
treks.network_coverage: BSNL works in Sankri. No network after Taluka. Satellite phone recommended for emergencies.

treks.name: Bhimbetka Rock Shelter Walk
treks.description: Walk through UNESCO rock shelters with 30,000-year-old cave paintings.

treks.name: Prashar Lake Trek
treks.description: A serene alpine lake at 2730m with a floating island and ancient pagoda-style temple dedicated to Sage Prashar. The trail winds through cedar forests with panoramic views of Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal ranges. Perfect weekend trek from Delhi or Chandigarh — doable as a day hike or overnight camp.
highlights: Floating island in the lake that moves position
Cedar and oak forests with wildflowers in spring
Night camping by the lake under stars
warnings: Road to Baggi village can be rough in monsoon
Lake edge is slippery — stay on marked paths
No food stalls after Baggi — carry your own
Temperatures drop sharply after sunset even in summer
Mobile network is patchy — inform someone before starting

day_by_day_first.meals: Carry packed lunch and snacks. Tea available at temple sometimes. Dinner self-cooked if camping.
day_by_day_first.title: Baggi Village to Prashar Lake and Return
day_by_day_first.water: Stream crossings on trail. Lake water needs purification. Carry 2L.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Well-defined trail through dense cedar forest, moderate incline for first 3km then gradual
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Mandi to Baggi village (35km, 1.5hrs). Trail starts at the end of the motorable road. Initial section through terraced fields, then enters dense cedar forest. Steady climb with occasional views of Beas valley. Temple and lake appear suddenly after final ridge. Explore the temple, circumambulate the lake, and return same route. Camping overnight possible near the lake.

treks.nearest_hospital: Zonal Hospital Mandi — 35km from Baggi village, 1.5 hours by road
treks.network_coverage: BSNL weak at lake. Jio/Airtel available till Baggi village. No reliable signal at campsite.

treks.name: Living Root Bridge Trek (Nongriat)
treks.description: Descend 3500 hand-carved stone steps into a lush subtropical canyon to reach Nongriat village and its legendary Double Decker Living Root Bridge — a UNESCO-nominated marvel grown over centuries by the Khasi people from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees. The natural swimming pool below the bridge is a perfect reward. One of the most unique treks on the planet.
highlights: Double Decker Living Root Bridge — centuries-old living architecture
3500 stone steps carved into the hillside
Natural swimming pool with crystal-clear water
Lush subtropical canyon with betel nut and areca palms
warnings: 3500 steps down means 3500 steps back UP — the ascent is demanding
Steps are slippery when wet — grip shoes essential
Very hot and humid in the canyon — carry 3L water
The ascent back takes significantly longer than descent
Monsoon months make steps dangerously slippery

day_by_day_first.meals: Basic meals available in Nongriat village
day_by_day_first.title: Tyrna to Nongriat and back
day_by_day_first.water: Streams in canyon, carry 3L from Tyrna
day_by_day_first.terrain: 3500 stone steps descent into canyon, same route return. Steep and demanding on return.
day_by_day_first.campsite: None for day trek. Homestays available if staying overnight.
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Tyrna village (1200m). Begin descending the famous 3500 steps through subtropical vegetation. Cross steel wire bridges over rushing streams. Reach Nongriat village and the Double Decker Living Root Bridge. Explore the natural swimming pool. Visit the nearby single root bridge. Begin the grueling ascent back to Tyrna.

treks.nearest_hospital: Cherrapunji CHC — 12km from Tyrna, 30 minutes by road. Shillong Civil Hospital — 80km, 3 hours.
treks.network_coverage: Jio works at Tyrna. No coverage in the canyon/Nongriat. Signal returns on ascent.

treks.name: Ratangad Fort Trek
treks.description: A Sahyadri fort with a natural rock window (Nedhe — the eye of the needle) that frames the surrounding hills perfectly. The trek from Ratanwadi village passes Amruteshwar temple (12th century Hemadpanthi architecture) and climbs through forest to the fort.
highlights: Nedhe — natural rock window with framed Sahyadri views
Views of Bhandardara lake and Kalsubai
Rock patch near summit — thrilling scramble
warnings: Rock patch requires scrambling — not for beginners

treks.name: Visapur Fort Trek
treks.description: Larger and less crowded than neighbouring Lohagad. Visapur Fort has ruins of old buildings, cannon placements, and a waterfall inside the fort during monsoon. Connected to Lohagad via a saddle — do both in a day for the full experience.
highlights: Connected to Lohagad for double fort trek

treks.name: Laka Glacier Trek
treks.description: A lesser-known extension beyond Triund that takes you into the raw Dhauladhar range. Laka Glacier sits in a dramatic amphitheater of rock and ice at 3200m, with massive boulders, moraines, and a seasonal glacial lake. Far fewer trekkers make it here compared to Triund, giving it a wild, remote feel just hours from McLeodganj.
highlights: Far fewer crowds than Triund — raw wilderness
Close-up views of Dhauladhar rock faces
warnings: Trail beyond Triund is unmarked — easy to get lost
Weather deteriorates fast at glacier — morning visits only
No camping infrastructure at glacier — camp at Laka Got
Snow and ice patches even in summer near glacier
Not a good trek in monsoon — rockfall risk

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Triund tea shops. Dinner at camp (self-cooked or operator).
day_by_day_first.title: McLeodganj to Triund to Laka Got
day_by_day_first.water: Chai shops on Triund trail. Stream at Laka Got.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Triund trail (well-marked) then beyond into unmarked rocky terrain. Steep sections after Triund.
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Galu Devi Temple. Follow Triund trail through forest (9km, 5hrs). At Triund, continue beyond — trail becomes faint. Cross rocky ground heading towards the Dhauladhar wall. Camp at Laka Got — a flat area with stream water before the glacier moraine begins.

treks.nearest_hospital: Dharamshala Zonal Hospital — 10km from McLeodganj, 30 minutes by road
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel work till Triund (weak). No signal beyond Triund. Zero coverage at Laka Got/glacier.

treks.name: Phulara Ridge Trek
treks.description: One of the few ridge walks in India where you spend most of the trek walking along a high ridge with continuous Himalayan views rather than in valleys. Phulara Ridge runs parallel to the Kedarkantha massif, offering non-stop views of Swargarohini, Black Peak, Bandarpoonch, and Ruinsara peaks. The trail crosses lush meadows with wildflowers and ancient shepherds' camps.
highlights: Continuous ridge walk with non-stop Himalayan panorama
Wildflower meadows rival Valley of Flowers
Ancient shepherd trails and seasonal settlements
Far less crowded than Kedarkantha or Har Ki Dun
warnings: Inner Line Permit required from Uttarkashi
Ridge is exposed — no shelter from wind or rain
Weather can close in quickly — carry storm gear
Trail is less established — guide essential
No water on ridge sections — carry 3L minimum
Bears in forest sections — travel in groups

day_by_day_first.meals: Packed lunch. Dinner at camp.
day_by_day_first.title: Sankri to Taluka to Pushtara
day_by_day_first.water: Stream at Pushtara. Fill up — next water is hours away.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail ascending through pine and oak to meadow. Moderate gradient.
day_by_day_first.description: Drive to Sankri, then short drive to Taluka. Trek begins climbing through pine forest along a stream. At 2400m transition to oak and birch forest. Trail opens at Pushtara — a beautiful meadow campsite with first ridge views.

treks.nearest_hospital: District Hospital Uttarkashi — 95km from Sankri, 4 hours by road
treks.network_coverage: BSNL in Sankri (weak). No network on ridge. Completely off-grid for 3 days.

treks.name: Stok Kangri Trek
treks.description: India's most popular 6000er and the highest trekkable peak in the country without mountaineering certification. At 6153m, Stok Kangri is a serious high-altitude endeavor — the summit push involves glacier travel, steep snow slopes, and extreme cold. The reward is standing on top of a 6000m peak with views stretching from the Karakoram to the Zanskar range. Not for the faint-hearted.
highlights: Summit a 6000m peak without mountaineering certification
Panoramic views of Karakoram, Zanskar, and Ladakh ranges
Glacier travel and steep snow climbing experience
Base camp in stunning Stok valley below the peak
Achievement of a lifetime for serious trekkers
warnings: Extreme altitude — AMS, HACE, HAPE are real risks. Acclimatize 3-4 days in Leh first
Summit success rate is only 40-50% — weather and fitness dependent
Temperatures drop to -20C on summit night
Glacier crevasses present — roped climbing required
Guide and high-altitude porters absolutely mandatory
Diamox recommended — consult doctor before trek
This is a mountaineering expedition, not a casual trek
Physical training for 3-6 months before attempting is essential

day_by_day_first.meals: Packed lunch. Dinner at camp prepared by cook.
day_by_day_first.title: Leh to Stok Village to Chang Ma
day_by_day_first.water: Stok Nala runs alongside trail. Reliable.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Valley trail along Stok Nala. Gradual ascent on well-defined path.
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Leh to Stok village (15km, 30min). Trek begins along the Stok Nala (stream). Gentle valley walk through arid Ladakhi landscape with willow trees. Pass small shepherd huts. Reach Chang Ma campsite at 4300m. Rest and hydrate.

treks.nearest_hospital: SNM Hospital Leh — 15km from Stok village, 30 minutes. Altitude rescue by Indian Army/ITBP on request.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel in Leh and Stok village. No network above Stok village. Satellite phone essential for expedition.

treks.name: Kudremukh Peak Trek
treks.description: Trek to the horse-face peak through rolling grasslands in Kudremukh National Park. One of the most scenic treks in Western Ghats.
treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Kalasa 25km. Government Hospital Sringeri 45km.
treks.network_coverage: No coverage inside the national park. Jio at Mullodi village.

treks.name: Mawryngkhang Bamboo Trail
treks.description: One of Meghalaya's most thrilling trails, Mawryngkhang takes you across bamboo bridges suspended over a 1000-foot gorge and along cliff-edge paths to a rocky pinnacle. The Wahthyllong bamboo bridge — rebuilt annually by villagers — is the centerpiece, swaying as you cross high above the valley. Not for the faint-hearted, but the views and adrenaline are unmatched in Northeast India.
highlights: Cliff-edge trail with dramatic valley views
Wahthyllong bamboo bridge — rebuilt every year
Rocky pinnacle viewpoint at the end
One of India's most thrilling day treks
warnings: Absolutely not suitable for anyone with vertigo or fear of heights
Bamboo bridges are narrow and sway — grip shoes essential
Trail is exposed and dangerous in rain or wind
No safety railings on cliff sections
Turn back if conditions are wet — bridges become extremely slippery

day_by_day_first.meals: Carry snacks — nothing available
day_by_day_first.title: Wahkhen to Mawryngkhang Pinnacle
day_by_day_first.water: Carry all water — none on trail
day_by_day_first.terrain: Stone steps, bamboo bridges over gorge, cliff-edge paths, rocky scramble to pinnacle
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Wahkhen village near Shillong. Descend stone steps into the gorge. Cross the famous Wahthyllong bamboo bridge suspended above the canyon. Navigate cliff-edge trails with exposure on both sides. Scramble up rocks to the Mawryngkhang pinnacle for panoramic views. Return same route.

treks.nearest_hospital: Shillong Civil Hospital — 50km from Wahkhen, 2 hours by road.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Wahkhen village. No coverage on the trail.

treks.name: Shirui Peak Trek
treks.description: A gentle trek to Shirui Peak (2835m) in Manipur's Ukhrul district, home to the endemic Shirui Lily (Lilium mackliniae) — a flower found nowhere else on earth that blooms in May-June. The trail passes through meadows and pine forests with panoramic views of the Manipur hills. The Shirui Lily Festival in May draws visitors from across the Northeast.
highlights: Endemic Shirui Lily blooms May-June — found nowhere else on earth
Panoramic views of Manipur hills from 2835m
Tangkhul Naga cultural experience in Ukhrul
warnings: Best only in Apr-Jun when lily blooms — limited season
Weather can be foggy — views not guaranteed
Road to Ukhrul can be disrupted in monsoon

day_by_day_first.meals: Carry packed lunch
day_by_day_first.title: Shirui Village to Shirui Peak
day_by_day_first.water: Carry from village
day_by_day_first.terrain: Gentle forest trail through pine and meadows
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Shirui village near Ukhrul. Trail climbs gently through pine forest and open meadows. In May-June, the endemic Shirui Lily covers the upper slopes. Reach the peak for 360-degree views of Manipur hills. Return same route.

treks.nearest_hospital: Ukhrul District Hospital — 8km from Shirui village, 20 minutes by road.
treks.network_coverage: Airtel works in Ukhrul and Shirui village. Patchy on the peak.

treks.name: Tadiandamol Trek
treks.description: Highest peak in Coorg, easy day trek through coffee plantations and shola grasslands.
treks.nearest_hospital: Government Hospital Virajpet 20km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Nalknad Palace trailhead. No coverage on peak.

treks.name: Bali Pass Trek
treks.description: A challenging crossover trek connecting Har Ki Dun valley to Yamunotri via the formidable Bali Pass at 4950m. This trek combines the cultural charm of the Har Ki Dun trail with a serious high-altitude pass crossing involving steep snow and scree. The descent into the Yamunotri valley provides a completely different perspective of Garhwal. Essentially two great treks connected by a dramatic pass.
highlights: Connects Har Ki Dun and Yamunotri — two iconic valleys
Ancient villages of Osla and Seema
Views of Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch, and Kalanag
Far less crowded than either valley separately
warnings: Pass crossing requires crampons, ice axe, and rope
Steep snow wall on pass approach — guide mandatory
River crossings in Har Ki Dun valley can be tricky
Not suitable without prior high-altitude pass experience
Emergency evacuation from pass area is extremely difficult

day_by_day_first.meals: Packed lunch. Dinner at homestay.
day_by_day_first.title: Sankri to Taluka
day_by_day_first.water: Supin River alongside.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Gentle forest trail along Supin River.
day_by_day_first.description: Same as Har Ki Dun day 1. Follow Supin River through pine and oak forest to Taluka village.

treks.nearest_hospital: District Hospital Uttarkashi — 95km from Sankri (start), 80km from Yamunotri (end). No medical help for 4 days mid-trek.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL in Sankri and Osla (weak). Zero coverage days 3-5. BSNL returns at Yamunotri.

treks.name: Buran Ghati Trek
treks.description: One of the most thrilling moderate-to-hard crossover treks in Himachal. Buran Ghati involves a steep snow wall rappel at the 4572m pass — a unique experience not found on most Indian treks. The trail traverses from Shimla's green Pabbar valley to the arid Spiti-like landscapes on the other side, passing through forests, meadows, glacial lakes, and finally the dramatic pass.
highlights: Rappelling down a steep snow wall at the pass
Landscape transition — green valley to arid moonscape
Chandranahan Lake — sacred glacial lake at 4000m
Dense silver birch and maple forests
One of the few treks with a technical rappel section
warnings: Snow wall rappel is real — not for those with fear of heights
Operator with fixed ropes and safety equipment is mandatory
Pass is only crossable May-June and September-October
Weather at pass changes in minutes — carry storm gear
River crossings can be dangerous after rain
Not suitable without prior high-altitude experience

day_by_day_first.meals: Packed lunch. Dinner at camp.
day_by_day_first.title: Janglik to Dayara Thach
day_by_day_first.water: Stream runs through meadow. Reliable.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail through pine and maple. Gradual ascent on well-trodden path.
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Shimla to Janglik village via Rohru and Chirgaon (10hrs, 210km — start early). Trek from Janglik through dense pine forest. Trail follows a stream upward. Emerge at Dayara Thach — a vast meadow surrounded by peaks. Camp here.

treks.nearest_hospital: Civil Hospital Rohru — 60km from Janglik, 3 hours. For Barua side: Hospital Rampur — 100km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL in Janglik (weak). No network on trek. Mudh village has BSNL.

treks.name: Chandrakhani Pass Trek
treks.description: An ancient trade route connecting Kullu to Malana — the famously isolated village with its own parliament and laws. The pass at 3660m offers stunning views of Parvati valley, Deo Tibba, and Indrasan peaks. The descent to Malana village adds a fascinating cultural dimension — one of the most unique communities in the Himalayas with strict touch-me-not customs.
highlights: Ancient trade route to isolated Malana village
Views of Deo Tibba, Indrasan, and Parvati valley
Malana's unique culture — own parliament and ancient democracy
Dense forests of birch, oak, and rhododendron
Less commercial than nearby Kheerganga or Triund
warnings: Malana has strict no-touch customs — do not touch anyone, any wall, or any temple
Photography restricted in Malana — ask before shooting
Trail can be unclear after snowfall — guide recommended
Steep descent to Malana is hard on knees
Do not accept or buy any illegal substances
Bears sighted in forest sections occasionally

day_by_day_first.meals: Packed lunch. Dinner at camp.
day_by_day_first.title: Naggar to Rumsu to Chandrakhani Pass Base
day_by_day_first.water: Streams in forest. Spring near base camp.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Steep climb through village then dense forest. Trail well-defined but relentless uphill.
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Naggar (drive from Kullu 20km). Climb through Rumsu village past ancient temples. Enter dense oak and cedar forest. Trail climbs steadily — no flat sections. Emerge at a meadow below the pass. Camp here.

treks.nearest_hospital: Regional Hospital Kullu — 20km from Naggar, 45 minutes. From Malana side: Kasol PHC 15km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at Naggar. No network after Rumsu until Malana. Malana has weak BSNL sometimes.

treks.name: Taragarh Fort Trek
treks.description: Trek to Taragarh Fort (Star Fort) above Ajmer. One of India oldest hill forts. Panoramic views over Pushkar and Ana Sagar Lake.

treks.name: Dayara Bugyal Trek
treks.description: One of the largest and most beautiful high-altitude meadows in India. Dayara Bugyal is a massive expanse of rolling alpine grassland at 3400m that turns gold in autumn and gets carpeted in snow during winter. The views of Bandarpoonch, Draupadi Ka Danda, and Black Peak from the meadow are breathtaking. A relatively easy moderate trek suitable for beginners stepping up.
highlights: Massive alpine meadow — one of largest in India
Bandarpoonch and Draupadi Ka Danda peak views
Gentle gradients make it ideal for first moderate trek
warnings: Inner Line Permit required from Uttarkashi DM office
Weather turns suddenly at meadow — carry warm layers
No tree cover at bugyal — exposed to wind and sun
Snow makes trail harder to follow in winter — guide essential
Bears in forest sections — make noise while walking

day_by_day_first.meals: Packed lunch from Barsu. Dinner at campsite.
day_by_day_first.title: Barsu to Barnala Tal
day_by_day_first.water: Stream near Barnala Tal. Carry 2L from Barsu.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Forest trail through oak and rhododendron. Moderate incline with well-defined path.
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Uttarkashi to Barsu village (45km, 2hrs). Trek starts with a climb through dense oak forest. Trail is well-marked and gradually ascends. At 2500m, forest opens slightly. Reach Barnala Tal — a small seasonal lake surrounded by trees. Camp here overnight.

treks.nearest_hospital: District Hospital Uttarkashi — 45km from Barsu, 2 hours by road
treks.network_coverage: BSNL works in Barsu. No network at Barnala Tal or Dayara Bugyal. Satellite phone recommended.

treks.name: Kangla Pass Trek
treks.description: A demanding high-altitude crossover connecting Pin Valley in Spiti to Kullu via the Kangla Pass at 5500m. The trek traverses the Pin Valley National Park — home to snow leopards and ibex — before climbing to a dramatic pass with views of the Great Himalayan Range. The descent into Kullu valley is steep and wild. A genuine wilderness adventure for experienced high-altitude trekkers.
highlights: Cross from Spiti to Kullu over 5500m pass
Pin Valley National Park — snow leopard habitat
Views of Great Himalayan Range from the pass
Ibex herds commonly sighted on approach
Complete landscape transition — arid Spiti to green Kullu
warnings: Very high pass at 5500m — AMS risk severe
Snow on pass even in August — crampons essential
Guide mandatory — trail unmarked above Pin base
Steep descent on Kullu side is treacherous
River crossings in Pin Valley can be dangerous after rain

day_by_day_first.meals: Homestay meals.
day_by_day_first.title: Kaza to Mudh Village
day_by_day_first.water: Village water.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Vehicle drive.
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Kaza to Mudh — the last village in Pin Valley (45km, 2hrs). Acclimatize and prepare. Meet guide and porters. Beautiful Buddhist village.

treks.nearest_hospital: CHC Kaza (start side) 45km. Kasol PHC (end side). No medical help for 4 days mid-trek.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL in Mudh (weak). Zero coverage days 2-5. Returns near Kheerganga (weak Jio/Airtel).

treks.name: Markha Valley Trek
treks.description: The classic Ladakh trek — a complete immersion into the stark, beautiful high-altitude desert landscape with whitewashed villages, ancient monasteries, and two high passes. The Markha Valley connects Hemis National Park to the Indus Valley, crossing Kongmaru La at 5150m. You walk through a landscape that feels prehistoric — craggy peaks, turquoise streams, and Buddhist prayer flags at every turn.
highlights: Two high passes — Ganda La (4960m) and Kongmaru La (5150m)
Hemis National Park — snow leopard territory
Ancient monasteries and prayer flag-draped passes
Complete Ladakhi cultural immersion with local families
warnings: Two passes above 5000m — serious AMS risk. Acclimatize in Leh 3-4 days
River crossings can be thigh-deep in July-August — trekking sandals needed
No phone network for entire trek duration
Homestays are basic — squat toilets, no hot water
Carry cash — no ATMs or digital payment on trek
Sun is intense at altitude — cover all exposed skin
Afternoon winds in valley can be fierce

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch packed from Leh. Dinner at homestay — Ladakhi thukpa and skyu.
day_by_day_first.title: Spituk to Jingchan
day_by_day_first.water: Stream in valley. Taps at Jingchan.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Gradual climb up side valley. Rocky path through arid landscape.
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Leh to Spituk (8km). Cross Indus on bridge and enter side valley. Trail follows stream through barren but beautiful terrain. Jingchan is the last village before Ganda La. Homestay overnight.

treks.nearest_hospital: SNM Hospital Leh — accessible only at start (Spituk) and end (Shang Sumdo). No medical help on trek.
treks.network_coverage: Zero mobile coverage for entire trek. BSNL at Spituk and Shang Sumdo only. Satellite phone recommended.

treks.name: Sandakphu Trek
treks.description: The only place on Earth where you can see four of the five highest peaks in the world in a single panorama — Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, and Makalu. Sandakphu at 3636m is the highest point in West Bengal, sitting right on the India-Nepal border. The trail passes through rhododendron forests that explode in red during April and the famous sleeping Buddha silhouette of the Kanchenjunga range.
highlights: Four of world's five highest peaks visible from summit
Sleeping Buddha silhouette of Kanchenjunga at sunrise
Sunrise view from Sandakphu — once seen never forgotten
warnings: Trek crosses into Nepal briefly — carry ID proof
Accommodation is basic trekkers huts — no luxury
Food options limited — Nepali dal-bhat is the staple
Cold nights even in October — carry proper warm layers
Land Rover option exists but misses the point of the trek

day_by_day_first.meals: Lunch at Meghma. Dinner at Tumling lodge — Nepali thukpa and dal-bhat.
day_by_day_first.title: Manebhanjan to Tumling
day_by_day_first.water: Streams and taps at Chitrey and Meghma. Tumling has piped water.
day_by_day_first.terrain: Steep initial climb on jeep track through forest. Rocky path with moderate gradient.
day_by_day_first.description: Drive from Darjeeling to Manebhanjan (26km, 1hr). Trek starts with a steep climb through Chitrey village. Pass through bamboo and rhododendron forest. Cross into Singalila National Park at Meghma. Tumling sits right on the India-Nepal border with first views of Kanchenjunga.

treks.nearest_hospital: Darjeeling District Hospital — 26km from Manebhanjan, 1 hour by road
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel work at Tumling (weak). No network at Kalipokhri. Intermittent at Sandakphu summit. BSNL best.

treks.name: Phawngpui Peak Trek
treks.description: A trek to the highest point in Mizoram — Phawngpui (Blue Mountain) at 2157m. The gentle trail through Phawngpui National Park passes through rhododendron and orchid forests with panoramic views extending to Myanmar. The peak is sacred to the Mizo people, and local legends surround the mountain. One of the easiest high-point treks in Northeast India.
highlights: Rhododendrons and orchids in spring bloom
One of the easiest state high-point treks in India
warnings: Weather can close views for days
Basic medical facilities in Thenzawl (nearest town)
Road access can be disrupted in monsoon

day_by_day_first.meals: Carry packed lunch
day_by_day_first.title: Park Gate to Phawngpui Peak
day_by_day_first.water: Carry from base — no reliable sources on trail
day_by_day_first.terrain: Gentle forest trail through rhododendron and bamboo
day_by_day_first.description: Start from Phawngpui National Park gate. Trail winds through dense rhododendron and orchid forest. Cross bamboo groves and open meadows. Final gentle ascent to the summit with views stretching into Myanmar. Return same route.

treks.nearest_hospital: Thenzawl Community Health Centre — 60km, 3 hours by road. Lunglei District Hospital — 100km.
treks.network_coverage: Patchy Jio/Airtel at the park gate. No coverage on the trail.

treks.name: Simlipal Waterfall Circuit
treks.description: Circuit through Simlipal biosphere visiting Barehipani Falls (217m) and Joranda Falls (181m). Forest roads + short walks to viewpoints.

treks.name: Skandagiri Night Trek
treks.description: Popular night trek near Bengaluru. Start at midnight, summit for sunrise. Rocky trail to a ruined fort.
treks.nearest_hospital: Government Hospital Chikkaballapur 20km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio at base. No coverage on hill.

treks.name: Kodachadri Trek
treks.description: Trek through dense Western Ghats rainforest to the misty peak. Spectacular sunset views of the Arabian Sea.
treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Kollur 25km. Government Hospital Shimoga 80km.
treks.network_coverage: No coverage on most of the trek. BSNL at Nittur base.

treks.name: Brahmagiri Peak Trek
treks.description: Trek through Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary on the Karnataka-Kerala border. Pristine shola forests and views into Wayanad.
treks.nearest_hospital: Government Hospital Virajpet 35km.
treks.network_coverage: No coverage in sanctuary. BSNL at Iruppu Falls entrance.

treks.name: Savandurga Hill Trek
treks.description: One of the largest monolith hills in Asia, 50km from Bengaluru. Rocky scramble up exposed granite face.
treks.nearest_hospital: Government Hospital Magadi 15km.
treks.network_coverage: Jio/Airtel at base.

treks.name: Yana Rocks Trek
treks.description: Short trek through dense forest to dramatic black limestone rock formations. The rocks look otherworldly.
treks.nearest_hospital: PHC Kumta 20km.
treks.network_coverage: Weak BSNL at Yana village.

treks.name: Dudhsagar Falls Trek
treks.description: Trek along abandoned railway tracks through Bhagwan Mahavir Sanctuary to India's 5th tallest waterfall. Cross bridges, wade through streams, and emerge at the 310m cascade.
warnings: Jeep track only — no private vehicles
treks.nearest_hospital: Sub-district Hospital Mollem 10km.
treks.network_coverage: No coverage on trail. BSNL at Collem.

treks.name: Fort Aguada Heritage Walk
treks.description: Walk through the 17th-century Portuguese fortress overlooking the Arabian Sea. Lighthouse, ramparts, and panoramic views of Sinquerim Beach.
treks.nearest_hospital: Goa Medical College Bambolim 20km.
treks.network_coverage: Full Jio/Airtel coverage.

treks.name: Netravali Wildlife Trek
treks.description: Trek through Netravali Wildlife Sanctuary to the Bubbling Lake (a natural carbonated spring) and Savari waterfall. Light jungle walk with birdwatching.
treks.nearest_hospital: Sub-district Hospital Quepem 20km.
treks.network_coverage: Weak signal inside sanctuary.

treks.name: Kumbhalgarh Great Wall Walk
treks.description: Walk along the 36km Kumbhalgarh Wall — 2nd longest wall in the world after China. Fort interior exploration included.

treks.name: Chembra Peak Trek
treks.description: Trek to Wayanad's highest peak past the viral heart-shaped lake. Rolling grasslands, shola forests, and panoramic views of the Western Ghats. The heart lake at the midpoint is one of Kerala's most photographed spots.
treks.nearest_hospital: Wayanad District Hospital Kalpetta 20km.
treks.network_coverage: No signal on trek. Jio at Meppady base.

treks.name: Meesapulimala Trek
treks.description: Trek to Kerala's second-highest peak through rolling grasslands and rhododendron forests. At 2,640m, the summit offers views of Tamil Nadu and Kerala simultaneously. The most rewarding multi-day trek in Kerala.
treks.nearest_hospital: Tata Hospital Munnar 30km.
treks.network_coverage: Zero coverage on trek.

treks.name: Agasthyarkoodam Trek
treks.description: Trek to the sacred peak of Agasthya Muni through the Neyyar Wildlife Sanctuary. One of Kerala's most challenging treks — steep ascents, dense forest, and a summit used by the Kani tribe for medicinal herb collection. Open only Jan-March.
treks.nearest_hospital: Trivandrum Medical College 75km.
treks.network_coverage: Zero. No signal.

treks.name: Ponmudi Golden Peak Trail
treks.description: Easy trail through montane forest to the Golden Peak viewpoint. Butterfly-rich path through cardamom and coffee. Perfect family trek with stunning views of the Agasthyamalai range.
treks.nearest_hospital: Trivandrum Medical College 55km.
treks.network_coverage: Decent Jio/Airtel.

treks.name: Periyar Tiger Trail (Jungle Patrol)
treks.description: A unique night-camping trek inside Periyar Tiger Reserve, guided by reformed poachers. Sleep in the forest, track wildlife, and experience the jungle at its most raw. One of India's most unique wildlife experiences.
treks.nearest_hospital: Kumily Hospital 10km.
treks.network_coverage: Zero inside reserve.

treks.name: Chembra Heart Lake Easy Trek
treks.description: Easy 2km trek from the permit point to the famous heart-shaped lake. The lake that broke the internet. Suitable for families — the trail is well-maintained and gentle. Stop at the lake, no need to continue to the peak.
treks.nearest_hospital: Wayanad District Hospital 20km.
treks.network_coverage: Weak signal at lake.

treks.name: Edakkal Cave Trek
treks.description: Short steep trek up to the prehistoric Edakkal Caves containing 8,000-year-old Mesolithic petroglyphs. One of the oldest human archaeological sites in South India. The cave is a natural cleft between two massive boulders.
treks.nearest_hospital: Wayanad District Hospital 15km.
treks.network_coverage: Good coverage.

treks.name: Ahobilam Upper Trail (9 Narasimha Temples)
treks.description: 8km one-way trek through dense Eastern Ghats forest gorge visiting all 9 Narasimha shrines.

treks.name: Athirapally-Vazhachal Forest Trail
treks.description: Easy forest trail connecting Athirapally Falls to Vazhachal Falls through dense Western Ghats evergreen forest. Best in monsoon when both waterfalls are in full flow. Birdwatching opportunities en route.
treks.nearest_hospital: Chalakudy Hospital 30km.
treks.network_coverage: Weak inside forest.

treks.name: Kodaikanal Dolphin Nose Trek
treks.description: Easy trek from Kodaikanal to Dolphin Nose viewpoint — a rock formation shaped like a dolphin's nose hanging over a 2,000ft valley. One of the most dramatic viewpoints in the Western Ghats.
warnings: Cliff edge — no railing at viewpoint
treks.nearest_hospital: Kodaikanal Hospital 5km.
treks.network_coverage: Decent coverage.

treks.name: Catherine Falls Trek
treks.description: Trek through tea estates to Catherine Falls — 250m double-tiered waterfall, one of the tallest in Tamil Nadu. The falls are named after the wife of a British collector. Best post-monsoon.
treks.nearest_hospital: Coonoor Hospital 20km.
treks.network_coverage: No signal on trek.

treks.name: Doddabetta Peak Trek
treks.description: Short walk to the highest point in the Nilgiris (2,637m). Telescope house at summit. On clear days, views stretch across three states.
treks.nearest_hospital: Ooty Hospital 10km.
treks.network_coverage: Good coverage.

treks.name: Valparai Sholayar Forest Trail
treks.description: Trek through Sholayar dam area and Anamalai forest. Lion-tailed macaque territory. Dense shola-grassland mosaic. Guided trek only.
treks.nearest_hospital: Pollachi Hospital 65km.
treks.network_coverage: No signal.

treks.name: Meghamalai Cloud Forest Trek
treks.description: Guided trek through cloud forest and tea estates in the High Wavy Mountains. Advance estate permission required. One of Tamil Nadu's most pristine forest walks.
treks.nearest_hospital: Theni Hospital 50km.
treks.network_coverage: Zero signal.

treks.name: Chettinad Heritage Mansion Walk
treks.description: Walking tour through Kanadukathan and Karaikudi villages visiting Chettinad mansions, Athangudi tile workshops, and cooking demonstrations. The best way to experience 10,000 mansions.
highlights: Burma teak and Italian marble architecture
warnings: Some mansions privately owned — permission needed
treks.nearest_hospital: Karaikudi Hospital 5km.
treks.network_coverage: Good coverage.

treks.name: Hogenakkal Coracle & Falls Trail
treks.description: Coracle ride through waterfalls followed by river fish fry and traditional oil massage. The complete Hogenakkal experience in one morning.
warnings: Not available when river is in flood
treks.nearest_hospital: Dharmapuri Hospital 45km.
treks.network_coverage: BSNL weak.

treks.name: Khandagiri-Udayagiri Caves Heritage Walk
treks.description: Walk through 2nd century BCE Jain rock-cut caves. Two adjacent hills with carved chambers, inscriptions, and elephant friezes.

treks.name: Girnar Hill Trek (10,000 Steps)
treks.description: 10,000 stone steps to the summit of Mount Girnar. Passes 16 Jain and Hindu temples. Starts at 4am for sunrise. One of India oldest pilgrimage treks.

treks.name: Saputara Sunset Point Trek
treks.description: Easy hill station walk to Sunset Point through tribal Dang forest. Gujarat only hill station.

treks.name: Shatrunjaya Hill Climb (863 Temples)
treks.description: 3,500 stone steps to 863 Jain temples on a single hilltop. The most concentrated sacred architecture on Earth.
warnings: Closes at sunset — time your visit
Doli carriers available for those who cannot walk

treks.name: Champaner Pavagadh Hill Trek
treks.description: Trek through UNESCO World Heritage ruins to Kalika Mata Temple at summit. Passes Mughal mosques and Hindu temples.

treks.name: Ranthambore Fort Heritage Trek
treks.description: Walk to the 10th-century Ranthambore Fort inside the tiger reserve. Ganesh temple, Jain temples, and panoramic views.
warnings: Inside tiger reserve — stay on path

treks.name: Guru Shikhar Summit Trek
treks.description: Short trek to Guru Shikhar — highest peak in the Aravalli Range and all of Rajasthan at 1,722m.

treks.name: Chitrakoot Parikrama Walk
treks.description: Sacred circumambulation of Kamadgiri hill — where Ram, Sita, and Lakshman lived during exile. Multiple temples en route.

treks.name: Haflong Hills Trek
treks.description: Trek through Assam only hill station. Haflong Lake, Jatinga (mysterious bird suicide point), Dimasa tribal areas.

treks.name: Rajgir Five Hills Circuit
treks.description: Walk the 5 hills surrounding Rajgir — each associated with Buddha. Hot springs, Griddhakuta (Vulture Peak), Japanese Stupa.

treks.name: Tiger Hill Sunrise Trek
treks.description: Pre-dawn trek (or drive) to Tiger Hill for sunrise over Kanchenjunga — the world 3rd highest peak. Golden light on snow.
warnings: Foggy days = no view — check forecast

treks.name: Sandakphu Approach Trek
treks.description: Trek to Sandakphu — highest point in West Bengal. See 4 of 5 highest peaks: Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, Makalu.
warnings: Cold at altitude — sleeping bag essential
